note.after_visit_summary: You are having a flare of your eczema (atopic dermatitis), likely due to the cold, dry air at your warehouse job. We are restarting a stronger prescription ointment, triamcinolone 0.1 percent, to apply twice daily to the affected areas on your elbows, knees, neck, and hands for two weeks, then only on weekends on spots that tend to return. Do not use it on your face or groin. Stop the over-the-counter hydrocortisone you were using. For nighttime itching that wakes you, take hydroxyzine 25 milligrams at bedtime as needed; it may make you sleepy, so do not drive after taking it. Continue taking your cetirizine 10 milligrams each morning for allergies. Moisturize well with a thick, fragrance-free cream or petroleum jelly at least twice a day and right after lukewarm showers. Wear cotton-lined gloves at work when you can to protect your skin. If you notice oozing, yellow crusts, or develop a fever, call us right away as this could mean infection. We will see you back in 4 weeks on Monday, November 2nd to check your skin.
